text: Stuart Warren (24 December 1938 – 22 March 2020) was a British organic chemist and author of chemistry textbooks designed for university students. He was educated at Cheadle Hulme School near Manchester and studied the Natural Sciences Tripos at Trinity College, Cambridge, where he completed a PhD under Malcolm Clark. He then moved to Harvard for post-doctoral research with F. H. Westheimer, after which he returned to Trinity as a research fellow. In 1971, he began a teaching fellowship at Churchill College. He remained a lecturer and researcher in the Department of Chemistry at Cambridge until his retirement in 2006. Warren received the Royal Society of Chemistry Bader Award in 2002, and following his death, the RSC published a themed collection of his work. His research group is recognized for producing many of the most successful organic chemistry academics in the UK. Warren is particularly known for his textbooks: Chemistry of the Carbonyl Group (1974), Designing Organic Syntheses: The Synthon Approach (1978), Organic Synthesis: The Disconnection Approach (first edition 1982, second edition 2008), and its graduate-level follow-up, Organic Synthesis: Strategy and Control (2007). He is best known as a co-author of the best-selling undergraduate text Organic Chemistry (first edition 2000, second edition 2012), which he wrote with his former students Jonathan Clayden and Nick Greeves, and fellow Cambridge lecturer Peter Wothers.
